name: pediatric seizures overview
title: A child with a seizure: ABCDE and a bedside glucose and blood gas for every child, then fever and the seizure's features sort a simple from a complex febrile seizure, and a seizure past 5 minutes is convulsive status epilepticus treated by the clock with benzodiazepines, then a second-line load, then the intensive care unit

root.title: Child seizing: ABCDE + time it
lines: EVERY child: bedside GLUCOSE + blood GAS with electrolytes
low glucose → IV dextrose (D10 5 mL/kg) · low sodium → 3% saline 3-5 mL/kg
subtle in newborns: lip smacking, eye deviation, bicycling, apnea, vital sign changes

groups.title: FEVER, age 6 months-5 years: FEBRILE seizure
lines: only if NO CNS infection, NO acute electrolyte problem, NO past afebrile seizure
WORRY: not back to baseline · meningeal signs or toxic look · delay or neurologic condition

groups.title: Still seizing at 5 MINUTES
lines: or no return to baseline between seizures

head: h
Simple febrile seizure
inv: if back to baseline, no other concern

head: h
Complex febrile seizure
inv: by time back to baseline, neurologic signs, family comfort
tx: counsel: can recur and become epilepsy

head: h
Convulsive status epilepticus
> 30 min, or 2+ seizures without recovery
pres: • longer = more brain injury: time matters
inv: • infection: blood count, CRP, cultures, CSF if stable
• head CT: head injury, focal signs, raised pressure
tx: • no IV access: sublingual lorazepam or intranasal midazolam
